 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER  Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.2977 of 2023(7) dt.16-04-2024  2/5 7 16-04-2024 1.
Since both these appeals have arisen out of the common judgement so appellants' prayer has been heard together and is being decided by this common order.
2. Heard the parties.
3. The matter has been placed for consideration on appellants' bail prayer made under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. and suspension of their sentence during the pendency of their appeal.

4. These appeals have been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 05.06.2023 and order of sentence dated 09.06.2023 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum Special Judge SC/ST Act, West Champaran, Bettiah in connection with Sessions Trial case No. 207/ 1993,
arising out of Chautarwa P.S. case No. 08 of 1992, whereby the appellants have been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 148, 323 and 376 (2)(g) of the IPC and under section 3(i)(xi)
of SC/ ST Act and sentenced for the said offences.

sentences.text: 5. Mr. Rama Kant Sharma, learned senior counsel for the appellants submits that admittedly, there was a land dispute in between the appellants and the so called victim, who has lodged the F.I.R., and in the F.I.R., no allegation of gang rape or Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.2977 of 2023(7)
dt.16-04-2024 physical assault upon the victim by the appellant, Surendra Dubey @ Benga Pandit was made and she remained mum regarding the said allegation while recording her re-statement and she recorded her statement under section 164 of the Cr. P. C. after ten months of the alleged occurrence in which she come up with a new allegation of gang rape and physical assault on her private part using the pointed part of a gun by the appellant, Surendra Dubey @ Benga Pandit.

It is further submitted that the allegations levelled by the victim in her statement recorded under section 164 of the Cr. P. C. particularly with regard to the allegations of gang rape and physical assault on her private part are completely unbelievable as one would definitely sustain serious injury when the pointed part of a gun is penetrated and encircled inside the private part of a female but in the present matter as per medical examination report of the victim, discussed in the impugned judgement, five injuries were found on person of the victim and all the said injuries were opined to be simple in nature and among these injuries one injury found on the inner surface of the left Labia majora was also opined to be simple in nature which falsifies the allegation of causing injury to the victim's private part by using the pointed part of a gun.

He further submits that all the appellants Gauri Shankar Choudhary @ Gauri Shankar ... vs The State Of Bihar on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100742814/

sentences.text:
APP (SJ) No.2977 of 2023(7) dt.16-04-2024 during trial period and their trial was completed in 32 years and they suffered a lot on account of such long period of their trial, which in itself is a kind of punishment upon them and during trial, none of them misused the privilege of bail and appellants, Gauri Shankar Chowdhary @ Gauri Choudhary,
Amar Singh Chowdhary, Parshuram Chowdhary and Shambhu Chowdhary are aged more than 60 years in the present time and the appellant Surendra Dubey @ Benga Pandit is 59 years old in the present time and there is no chance of early hearing of their appeals.

6. Mrs. Preeti Kumari, learned counsel appearing for the informant has vehemently opposed the bail prayer and submitted that the alleged incident took place in the year 1992 and at that time a victim belonging to Scheduled Caste did not dare to come up with the allegations against the strong persons and the victim in her initial version could not have explained all the details of events but later on she gave the details of all the events which happened with her and the most important thing which goes in favour of her allegations is the victim's medical examination which shows that she sustained injury on her private part and the said injury was proved before the trial court.
7.
Mr. Vinay Krishna, learned Spl. P. P. has also Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.2977 of 2023(7)
dt.16-04-2024 opposed the bail prayer of the appellants.

8. Considering the seriousness of the accusation appearing against the appellants and particularly,
taking into account the victim's injury report, this court is not inclined to accept the bail prayer of the appellants.
Accordingly, their bail prayer stands rejected.

9. As the appellants are old persons and they faced the trial for 32 years so considering this aspect,
both the appeals are directed to be listed under the heading "for hearing" on 15.07.2024.

(Shailendra Singh, J) BKS/-
